evidence_quotes.quote: Correction to: Factors associated with water service continuity for the Rural Populations of Bangladesh, Pakistan, Ethiopia, and Mozambique (Environmental Science and Technology (2019) 53:8 (4355-4363) DOI: 10.1021/acs.est.8b07173). Environmental Science and Technology, 53 (15). p. 9338.

there are several instances where we incorrectly reported predicted water service continuity (WSC) values as odds ratios (OR). We have provided a corrected version of the relevant text in the Results section below, with the updated text (i.e., WSC) shown in bold.

the model predicted higher WSC for tube wells/boreholes (WSC = 95%, CI = 75−99%), piped supply (WSC = 80%, CI = 47−95%), and other water sources (WSC = 88%, CI = 51−98%) compared to when ﬁnancial contributions were not made for tube wells/boreholes
the model predicted sources with good water appearance to have higher WSC for tube wells/boreholes (WSC = 97%, CI = 88−99%), dug wells (WSC = 98%, CI = 90−100%)

criterion_notes.c1: Satisfied from the title and corrected Results excerpts: the study examines rural water service continuity across tube wells/boreholes, piped supply, dug wells, springs, surface water, and other water sources.
criterion_notes.c2: Unclear because only a 1-page Addition/Correction (DOI: 10.1021/acs.est.9b03482) was retrieved rather than the 9-page main article (DOI: 10.1021/acs.est.8b07173). Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, the Pakistan snippet mentions comparing water service continuity when financial contributions were made versus not made, and the original article may also examine institutional, management, or governance factors, but without the full text we cannot verify how financial contributions or any governance variables are defined (plain reading = unclear / cannot_tell). Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading of Criterion 2, we likewise cannot determine without the full text whether financial contributions reflect a formal tariff or cost-recovery rule governing service access/continuity (eligible rule-type mechanism) versus voluntary community O&M contributions or generic project delivery, or whether other rule-type mechanisms are analysed (narrow reading = unclear / cannot_tell).
criterion_notes.c3: Unclear in the retrieved file: the corrected Results snippets report quantitative statistical model predictions with confidence intervals, indicating the underlying paper is empirical, but the retrieved 1-page erratum lacks the data description and empirical methods needed for methodological assessment.
criterion_notes.c4: Satisfied: the excerpts report predicted water service continuity (WSC), an outcome directly measuring water service continuity/reliability.
criterion_notes.c5: Unclear because the full text of the original article (pp. 4355-4363) is missing; unit of analysis, sample size, full exposure definitions, and study design cannot be identified from the 1-page correction notice alone.
criterion_notes.c6: Satisfied: the text is in English.

population_and_sample: Rural populations of Bangladesh, Pakistan, Ethiopia, and Mozambique (sample size and unit of analysis not reported in the retrieved correction notice)
exposure: Factors associated with water service continuity, including whether financial contributions were made, water source type, and water appearance (full variable definitions not reported in the retrieved correction notice)
rationale: WRONG_PAPER_MISMATCH / paper_mention_mismatch (corrigendum retrieved instead of main article; reason: "full text not accessible"): The retrieved 2-page PDF is the White Rose repository deposit of the 1-page Addition/Correction (DOI: 10.1021/acs.est.9b03482, Environ. Sci. Technol. 2019, 53(15), p. 9338) rather than the full text of the 9-page target article in the record metadata (DOI: 10.1021/acs.est.8b07173, Environ. Sci. Technol. 2019, 53(8), pp. 4355-4363). Although a corrected Results snippet for Pakistan mentions whether financial contributions were made in predicting water service continuity (WSC), the original article's full text is required to identify the study design, sample/unit of analysis, and full variable definitions, and to assess whether any analysed factor constitutes a Criterion 2 governance/institutional factor (under either the plain wording or the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type tariff/cost-recovery mechanism reading).
